title: The answer key changes font size, not typeface, and leaves the Courier New entries untouched
evidence: The problem statement asks the agent to make every data entry use "a single, consistent typeface". Typeface means font family. In the source, the only cells that break the family pattern are 9 cells in Courier New 16 (A10 'AIG/DKR', D10 'A. RIACH', I10 'ABRAMO/ZIVIC', L10 9/28/2001, O10 'swap', A12 'ENA', L12 'nymex', P12 'nx1', U12 'NG'). Every other cell is Antique Olive. On the rendered sheet these Courier cells are the obvious inconsistency. In the answer key gt_117_ref_0.xlsx, all 9 cells are still Courier New 16. Comparing source and answer key cell by cell shows only one kind of change: the size of rows 19–23 (A19:V23, the trade lines) goes from Antique Olive 14/16 to Antique Olive 12. No font family changes anywhere. So the answer key standardizes size and ignores typeface. The grader guidance tells the grader to judge whether the output is "logically equivalent to the reference answer.xlsx". An agent that follows the instruction (switches the Courier cells to Antique Olive, keeps sizes) will not match the answer key on any changed cell, and may be failed as having 'extra modifications'. An agent that copies the answer key does not meet the stated typeface requirement. The task contradicts itself on what is graded, and the score is a single 0/1.
confirmation: Verified that the GT changes no font family. Only sizes in A19:V23 change, and Courier New stays in A10/D10/I10/L10/O10/A12/L12/P12/U12, which contradicts the 'single typeface' wording under a binary reference-equivalence grader.
fix: Answer key: in xl/styles.xml the 8 cellXfs that used font 10 (Courier New 16 bold) now use font 15 (Antique Olive 16 bold, otherwise identical). The nine data entries A10, D10, I10, L10, O10, A12, L12, P12 and U12 are now Antique Olive like every other populated cell. Values, sizes, fills, borders, alignment, drawings and controls are unchanged. Added a grader-guidance note: typeface means font family, any single family passes, and font-size changes are optional.

title: Prompt asks to standardize 'typeface' across 'all data entries', whereas ground truth leaves Courier New entries unchanged and only changes font size (14pt/16pt to 12pt) in rows 19–23
evidence: In problem.py:1, the prompt instructs: "Standardize the font across all data entries so they ues a single, consistent typeface throughout. No content changes are required; this is a formatting cleanup only." No target typeface, font size, or cell range is specified anywhere in the prompt or environment. In the source workbook (assets/117_src_0.xlsx, sheet 'Deal Sheet for Printing (2)'), the upper form's filled-in data entries (A10 'AIG/DKR', D10 'A. RIACH', I10 'ABRAMO/ZIVIC', L10 '2001-09-28', O10 'swap', A12 'ENA', L12 'nymex', P12 'nx1', U12 'NG') use 'Courier New' 16pt Bold, while the lower table's data entries in rows 19–23 already use the 'Antique Olive' typeface (at 12pt, 14pt, and 16pt Bold), and description entries B32/B33 use 'Antique Olive' 6pt/14pt Regular. In the ground truth (gt_117_ref_0.xlsx), all 9 'Courier New' 16pt Bold data entries in rows 10 and 12 are left untouched as 'Courier New' 16pt Bold, while 58 cells in rows 19–23 (columns A–V, which already had the 'Antique Olive' typeface) have their font size changed from 14pt/16pt to 12pt Bold, and empty rows 24–30 of the same table are left at 'Antique Olive' 16pt Bold. Because the AI grader (problems-metadata.json grading_strategy.agentic_grader_params.grader_guidance, 'Evaluation Criteria') grades binary pass/fail (score 0 or 1) against the reference answer gt_117_ref_0.xlsx and penalizes modifications outside the reference scope ('over_edit_avoidance'), a competent agent that follows the literal instruction to standardize the typeface (e.g., changing the Courier New data entries in rows 10 and 12 to Antique Olive, or standardizing all data entries to a uniform font and size) will diverge from the reference workbook and risk failing the single-score check.
confirmation: Comparing source and GT cell by cell, the only changes are 18 valued cells in rows 19-23 going from 14/16pt to 12pt Antique Olive. The 9 Courier New cells in rows 10/12 are unchanged, so the reference diverges from the prompt's typeface instruction.
fix: Answer key: in xl/styles.xml the 8 cellXfs that used font 10 (Courier New 16 bold) now use font 15 (Antique Olive 16 bold, otherwise identical). The nine data entries A10, D10, I10, L10, O10, A12, L12, P12 and U12 are now Antique Olive like every other populated cell. Values, sizes, fills, borders, alignment, drawings and controls are unchanged. Added a grader-guidance note: typeface means font family, any single family passes, and font-size changes are optional.
